correctness.rationale: Parity character projection gives P_m(p)=2^{-m}sum_k binom(m,k)(1-2p)^{k(m-k)}, with P0=1. The unconditioned probabilities of one and two isolated vertices are q^{n-1}P_{n-1} and q^{2n-3}P_{n-2}, so exact conditioned covariance is q^{2n-3}(P_{n-2}P_n-qP_{n-1}²)/P_n². At p=1/2 the even-degree subspace has size 2^{(n-1)(n-2)/2}, giving the exact positive value. For even n, complement of even-degree graphs has all degrees odd; smallest edge count n/2 gives only perfect matchings, so P_n~(n-1)!!q^{n/2}, while P_{n-1}->1. The one-point square dominates the joint q^{2n-4}/(n-1), making the negative coefficient. For odd n the complete graph is even-degree, so P_n,P_{n-2}->1 and positive pair term dominates. n=4 direct even graph enumeration gives p³q²(2-3p)/(6p²-4p+1)² and unique zero 2/3. Independent rational brute enumerations of all graphs n=3,4,5 at p=1/2,2/3,4/5 agreed; source longer finite checker was inspected rather than trusted as proof.

value.rationale: A sharp sign reversal created by conditioning independent edges on global degree parity is a structurally motivated counterexample to naive positive-association intuition. The full parity split, fixed-order dense asymptotic coefficient and exact n=4 threshold clarify when global parity constraints reverse local dependence, beyond the classical even-graph model itself.

final_claim: For G(n,p) conditioned on all vertex degrees even and distinct isolation indicators, covariance at p=1/2 is 2^{4-2n}>0, while as p tends to 1 at fixed n it is negative asymptotic -(1-p)^{n-2}/((n-1)!!)^2 for even n>=4 and positive asymptotic (1-p)^{2n-3} for odd n>=3; even n has sign reversal, n=4 unique crossing p=2/3.
limitations: Even n≥4 guaranteed at least one crossing, uniqueness only n=4. Odd n positivity only at p=1/2 and near p=1.
Independent finite exact graph enumerations n<=5 do not substitute for complement perfect-matching proof.
